papers.title: Finite element analysis of stem migration after total hip replacement
papers.abstract: After total hip replacement, the primary and secondary implant stability is critical to ensure long-term success. Excessive migration of the femoral stem can cause implant loosening. In this work, a novel approach for the simulation of the femoral stem migration using the finite element method is presented. Currently, only a few mostly contact-based models exist for this purpose. Instead, a bio-active interface model is used for the bone-stem interface which transforms from the Drucker-Prager to the von Mises plasticity criterion during the osseointegration process. As the position of the implant generally stabilises within one week after the implantation, the migration and osseointegration simulations are decoupled. To understand the effects on the migration, various parameter combinations are examined and a sensitivity analysis is performed. The results indicate that the joint force and the adhesion parameter have the most substantial influence on the migration. Furthermore, the influence of the migration on the subsequent osseointegration process is explored for a numerical example. The proposed model is able to depict the femoral stem migration with values up to 0.27 mm, which are in the order of magnitude of clinically observed values. Further, the model is provided as an open-source Abaqus user material subroutine. Numerical simulation of the stem migration could assist in clinical decision-making by identifying optimal parameter combinations to improve implant stability.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接针对股骨柄迁移模拟，与用户研究方向中的髋关节植入物稳定性分析高度相关。
llm.why_not_core: Does not address additive manufacturing (AM) design or fabrication of femoral stems, focusing solely on numerical simulation of migration.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发一种模拟全髋关节置换后股骨柄迁移的有限元方法
summary_zh.method: 使用生物活性界面模型，结合Drucker-Prager和von Mises准则，解耦迁移和骨整合模拟
summary_zh.result: 发现关节力和粘附参数对迁移影响最大，模拟迁移值达0.27 mm，与临床观察一致
summary_zh.validation: 通过数值算例与临床观察值对比验证

summary_en.motivation: Develop a finite element approach to simulate femoral stem migration after total hip replacement to assess implant stability.
summary_en.method: A bio-active interface model transitioning from Drucker-Prager to von Mises plasticity is used, with decoupled migration and osseointegration simulations.
summary_en.result: Joint force and adhesion parameter have the most substantial influence on migration, with values up to 0.27 mm, consistent with clinical observations.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation case compared to clinically observed migration magnitudes.
